```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

`statgen` stores each analysis object on a shared reference SNP axis. The R
package loads reference panels, summary statistics, annotations, genotypes, and
LD panels into those coordinates.

```{r}
library(statgen)
set_verbosity("quiet")
```

We use `quiet` to hide progress messages and loading summaries. Warnings remain
visible.

## Reference, Sumstats, And Annotations

The bundled package fixtures are intentionally tiny so that examples and CRAN
checks do not require external tools or large data.

This vignette reads those installed fixtures with
`system.file(..., package = "statgen")`. They are demonstration inputs only. In
real analyses, replace these paths with post-harmonization reference, summary
statistics, annotation, genotype, and LD files prepared for one analysis input
set. For an end-to-end repository workflow that prepares source inputs and then
runs the same R analysis pattern on those files, see
`docs/TUTORIAL_1_PREPARE_DATA.md` and `docs/TUTORIAL_4_R.md`.

```{r}
reference_template <- file.path(
  dirname(system.file("extdata", "reference_chr1.bim", package = "statgen")),
  "reference_chr@.bim"
)
reference <- load_reference(reference_template)

sumstats_path <- system.file("extdata", "traits_complete.tsv.gz", package = "statgen")
sumstats <- load_sumstats(sumstats_path, reference)

annotation_paths <- system.file(
  "extdata",
  c("anno1.bed", "anno2.bed"),
  package = "statgen"
)
binary_annotations <- load_annotations(annotation_paths, reference)
grouped_annotations <- load_annotation(
  system.file("extdata", "grouped.annot", package = "statgen"),
  reference,
  has_header = TRUE,
  group_column = "group"
)

continuous_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".annot")
writeLines(c(
  "chrom\tstart0\tend0\tscore",
  "1\t99\t200\t0.5",
  "1\t299\t400\t1.5",
  "X\t99\t301\t2.5"
), continuous_path)
continuous_annotations <- load_annotation(
  continuous_path,
  reference,
  has_header = TRUE,
  value_columns = "score"
)
annotations <- union_annotations(
  union_annotations(binary_annotations, grouped_annotations),
  continuous_annotations
)

num_snp(reference)
head(logpvec(sumstats))
colnames(annomat(annotations))
is_binary(annotations)
annotation_metadata(annotations)[!is_binary(annotations)]
```

R-native object caches are RDS files. They are useful for repeated analyses in
the same R runtime.

```{r}
sumstats_cache <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
save_sumstats_cache(sumstats, sumstats_cache)
sumstats_cached <- load_sumstats_cache(sumstats_cache)
identical(is_present(sumstats_cached), is_present(sumstats))
```

## Allele Alignment

Loaders default to `match_by = "genomic_position"`, matching positions and
alleles. This chrX example enables indel swaps in that mode. See
`?allele_matching` for allele roles, matching options, and cache behavior.

```{r}
swap_root <- system.file("extdata", "allele_swaps", package = "statgen", mustWork = TRUE)
swap_reference <- load_reference(file.path(swap_root, "reference.bim"), shards = "X")
swap_stats <- load_sumstats(file.path(swap_root, "sumstats.tsv.gz"), swap_reference,
                            allow_indel_swaps = TRUE)
swap_genotype <- load_genotype(file.path(swap_root, "genotype", "@"), swap_reference,
                               allow_indel_swaps = TRUE)
eaf_vec(swap_stats)
is_allele_swapped(swap_genotype)
fetch_genotypes_int8(swap_genotype, c(1, 3, 1))
```

`eaf_vec()` gives the frequency of the reference panel's `a1` (ALT) allele,
and `fetch_genotypes_int8()` counts copies of that allele.
`is_allele_swapped()` shows which variants required count inversion.

To select marker IDs instead of positions, both loaders accept
`match_by = "id"`; allele matching is still required. For example:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
trait_by_id <- load_sumstats(path, reference, match_by = "id")
genotype_by_id <- load_genotype(bfile_prefix, reference, match_by = "id")
```

ID mode supports non-palindromic SNVs, including strand complements. Comparison
is case-sensitive: `rs123` and `RS123` do not match. Sumstats require `SNP`,
the allele columns, and `P` and ignore coordinates, searching all source rows;
genotypes search only the corresponding chromosome. Reference ID/allele keys
are checked for ambiguity across the supplied panel in both loaders. See
`?allele_matching` for eligibility and duplicate handling.

## LD Panels

Python builds the canonical LD `.npz` distribution. For package examples,
`ld_root` points to a bundled toy distribution that already includes the R
reference-cache sidecar. For real analyses, run `prepare_ld_npz_for_r()` once
on the Python-built `ld_npz/` directory for the same harmonized input set, then
load that directory with `load_ld()`.

```{r}
ld_root <- system.file("extdata", "ld", package = "statgen")
ld <- load_ld(ld_root)

num_snp(ld)
a1freq(ld)
```

`multiply_r2()` multiplies aligned vectors or matrices by LD `r^2`.
`fast_prune()` applies greedy LD pruning to aligned scores.

```{r}
scores <- seq_len(num_snp(ld))
multiply_r2(ld, scores)

logp <- rev(seq_len(num_snp(ld)))
fast_prune(logp, ld, r2_threshold = 0.35)
```

## Genotype Metadata And Fetching

Genotype panels read calls from PLINK BED files when you request them. Keep
those files available; if you move them, supply their new location with
`bed_path`. A replacement file must keep the same variants, samples, and allele
order. Counts use the usual 0/1/2 scale; use `haploid_mode = "ploidy_scaled"`
to adjust for biological ploidy, such as male chrX. See `?allele_matching` for
allele orientation and BED overrides.

```{r}
ref_chr1 <- load_reference(system.file("extdata", "reference_chr1.bim", package = "statgen"))
bed_chr1 <- system.file("extdata", "genotype_1.bed", package = "statgen")
genotype <- load_genotype(sub("\\.bed$", "", bed_chr1), ref_chr1)

geno <- fetch_genotypes_int8(genotype, c(1, 3))
dim(geno)
head(geno)
```
